segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they gave a dinner for him there. Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Mary took a pound of perfume—pure nard, very costly—and anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, the one who was going to hand him over, said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this not because he cared about the poor but because he was a thief; he kept the money box and used to take what was put into it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a large crowd of the Jews learned that he was there, and they came not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The next day the large crowd that had come to the festival, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: took palm branches and went out to meet him, and they were shouting,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His disciples did not understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept testifying.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was also why the crowd went to meet him: they had heard that he had done this sign.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You see that you are getting nowhere. Look, the world has gone after him!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the festival.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: These came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and made a request of him:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Philip went and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever loves their life loses it, and whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone serves me, they must follow me, and where I am, there my servant will be also. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now my soul is troubled, and what should I say? ‘Father, save me from this hour’? But it was for this very reason that I came to this hour.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Father, glorify your name.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a voice came from heaven:

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “An angel has spoken to him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This voice came not for my sake but for yours.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this to indicate what kind of death he was going to die.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the crowd answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We have heard from the Law that the Messiah remains forever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The light is among you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you. Whoever walks in the darkness does not know where they are going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said these things, then went away and hid himself from them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Though he had done so many signs in front of them, they did not believe in him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that the word that Isaiah the prophet spoke would be fulfilled:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This is why they were unable to believe, because Isaiah also said:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Isaiah said these things because he saw his glory and spoke about him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nevertheless, many even among the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they would not confess it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for they loved the glory that comes from people more than the glory that comes from God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus cried out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever believes in me believes not in me but in the one who sent me,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have come into the world as light, so that everyone who believes in me would not remain in the darkness.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge that person, for I did not come to judge the world but to save the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words has a judge: the word that I have spoken will judge that person on the last day.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I have not spoken on my own; the Father who sent me has himself given me a command—what to say and what to speak.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And I know that his command is eternal life. So what I speak, I speak just as the Father has told me.”

notes.note: The measure is the Roman pound, about twelve ounces or a little under 330 grams. Nard was an imported aromatic oil. The price Judas names in verse 5, three hundred denarii, was roughly a year’s wages for a laborer, since a denarius was a common day’s pay.

The Greek adjective is rare and its exact meaning is uncertain. Most scholars take it as “genuine” or “unadulterated”, which is followed here. Other proposals are that it names the plant or place the nard came from, or that it means “liquid”. The same phrase occurs in Mark 14:3.

Most English versions say “betray” when Judas is the subject. The Greek verb is the ordinary word for handing someone into another’s custody, and the Gospels use it equally of the priests and of Pilate. “Hand over” lets the reader see that chain; the treachery is supplied by the context. Some scholars defend “betray” as a legitimate contextual sense for Judas.

notes.phrase: used to take what was put into it
notes.note: The verb ordinarily means “carry”, and the clause could say only that Judas carried the common funds. In the Greek of the period it was also used for carrying off or pilfering. After “he was a thief” that sense is likely, and most modern translations adopt it.

notes.phrase: so that she may keep it for the day of my burial
notes.traditional: against the day of my burying hath she kept this
notes.note: The Greek is compressed and its sense is disputed. It may mean “let her keep it” (what remains) for the burial. Or it may be elliptical: she did not sell it so that she could keep it for this purpose, with the anointing itself anticipating the burial. Some later manuscripts smooth the wording to “she has kept it”.

The word is a Hebrew cry meaning “save, please”, taken from Psalm 118:25. By the first century it was used as a shout of acclamation. The crowd’s words draw on Psalm 118:25–26, a psalm sung at the pilgrim festivals, and add “the king of Israel”. Palm branches were associated with national celebration and victory.

In Jewish usage “eternal life” is the life of the age to come, different in kind as well as unending. The word for “life” in this phrase is not the same as the “life” that is loved or hated earlier in the verse. That earlier word means a person’s present life or living self, which can be clung to and lost.

notes.phrase: Father, save me from this hour
notes.traditional: Father, save me from this hour
notes.note: Ancient manuscripts had no punctuation. The words may be a hypothetical prayer that Jesus considers and sets aside, as punctuated here, or an actual prayer that he then corrects with “But it was for this very reason…”. Translations and commentators are divided.

The verb means both to raise physically and to exalt. John uses it with both senses at once: Jesus is raised up on the cross, and the cross is his exaltation. Verse 33 makes the reference to crucifixion explicit. Some manuscripts read “all things” in place of “all people”.

The traditional rendering is “the Christ”. Here the crowd is debating what the expected anointed king will be like, so the word is a title, not a name, and “Messiah” conveys that to a modern reader. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels.

“The Law” here stands for the Scriptures as a whole, not only the books of Moses. No single passage says this in so many words. The crowd is probably thinking of promises that David’s line and kingdom will endure forever, such as Psalm 89:36.

The quotation in verse 40 comes from Isaiah 6, where the prophet sees the Lord enthroned in the temple. John says that the glory Isaiah saw there was that of Jesus, who is the “him” of this verse. Some manuscripts read “when he saw” in place of “because he saw”.

candidates.reason: With δοξάζω it runs through John and the letters, sometimes meaning divine splendor and sometimes human honor or praise (as in v. 43), and the wordplay is lost if the English varies without a rule.
John’s term for Jesus’s significant deeds is rendered “miracle” in some versions and “sign” in others, and it should be uniform across the Gospels, Acts and Revelation.
A key Johannine word group (with μαρτυρία, μάρτυς) that versions split between “testify”, “bear witness” and “witness”; readers need one rendering to follow the theme.
A thematic verb in John and 1 John rendered variously “abide”, “remain”, “stay” and “continue”; the links between passages depend on one English word.
It carries a deliberate double sense of lifting up and exalting in John (3:14, 8:28, 12:32–34) and means “exalt” elsewhere (Acts, Philippians, the Synoptics), so the split needs a rule.

warnings: Verse 11: πιστεύω is not rendered with a register form (believe / trust) and has no register-exception note.
